clue.text: Wild Cherry hosts a lot of wild parties, Sheraton style

indicators.note: the cherry tree hosts, or holds inside it, the trimmed parties

parts.note: the gean is the European wild cherry tree

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the word for parties loses its last letters

parts.note: orgies are wild parties

explanation.surface: A wild cherry tree somehow plays host to riotous parties in the manner of an elegant furniture maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer, so 'Sheraton style' points to the period of the four King Georges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheraton furniture dates from the reign of the four Georges, so his style belongs to that era.

clue.text: The big heat makes Spooner hear birdsong at twilight

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: to warble is to sing as a bird does
gloaming is a Scots and poetic word for dusk

explanation.surface: A Spooner remark turns birds singing at dusk into talk of a hot climate.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening syllables WAR and GLO of 'warble gloaming' to hear 'global warming'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising world temperatures are the great heating problem that the puzzle's theme keeps describing.

clue.text: Exaggerate government's position?

explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to claim too much; read as two words, a government sits over the state it runs.

clue.text: Immature lot of MPs waffle on, adding to the big heat

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced
the House of Commons is the body of British MPs
to gas is to chatter idly, so he gases means he waffles on

explanation.surface: Inexperienced parliamentarians talk endlessly, contributing to the climate crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament; their chamber is the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide, methane and similar emissions trap heat and so add to climate change.

clue.text: Old" is about about 1st century

indicators.note: the second about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: anent is an old word meaning concerning
I is the Roman numeral one, standing for first

explanation.surface: A quoted word is said to concern the first hundred years AD.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'about's do different jobs: the first gives ANENT, the second says CI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient things belong to the distant past, which is what old describes.

clue.text: A sign this way

parts.note: a cross is a written sign or mark

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sign pointing in this direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this way' refers to the clue itself, an across entry in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Across clues run left to right, the direction this one is read.

clue.text: Motor? Good to walk. Publish how you stand vis-a vis the big heat

definitions.text: how you stand vis-a vis the big heat

parts.note: a motor is a car
bon is French for good
to foot it is to walk
to print is to publish

explanation.surface: Advice to ditch the car and walk, then report your environmental standing.
explanation.walkthrough: BON is French, a common crossword source for 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: This measures the greenhouse emissions a person causes, their standing on climate change.

clue.text: Musical more central to order of drug

indicators.note: central to means placed in the middle of the order's letters

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
piu is the Italian musical direction for more

explanation.surface: A muddled phrase about music being central to drug orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' marks 'more' as a score direction, in Italian; the OM is the British Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic extracted from poppies.

clue.text: Unhappy about naughty Ariel being on the pay roll

indicators.note: about means the gloomy word wraps round the rearranged name

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of Ariel misbehave and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy about a mischievous sprite getting a wage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel, the sprite in Shakespeare's Tempest, is only anagram fodder here; 'naughty' rearranges the name before 'about' wraps the gloomy word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone salaried is paid a regular wage by an employer.

clue.text: Fuel carrier shows respect to the Queen

parts.note: one bows to show respect
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tanker driver bows to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowser is a fuel tanker, as on airfields.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowser is a tanker lorry that delivers petrol or water.

clue.text: Too fat to get medals for energy

parts.note: OBEs are honours awarded in Britain
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is too overweight to be honoured for vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesity is being seriously overweight.

clue.text: Singer in church getting round irish soldier on both sides

parts.note: O is round in shape
a GI is an American soldier
right and left, R and L, are both sides

explanation.surface: A singer in church encircles an Irish soldier on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on both sides' gives R and L, right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female chorister is one who sings in a church choir.

clue.text: I give place to a playwright for starters — they aren't there

indicators.note: give place to says the letter I steps aside so that the letter a takes its spot

parts.note: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright
in golf the tees are where each hole starts

explanation.surface: Someone yields to a dramatist at the opening of a show, though nobody turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I give place to a' changes Ibsen's I into A, making ABSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees are people missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Shellfish wanted — the previous one was a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter loses its starting letter here

parts.note: the former is the previous one of two

explanation.surface: A diner wants shellfish because the last one fell through.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an abalone, eaten in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an edible sea snail, a kind of abalone.

clue.text: Very old, in transport, prance about

indicators.note: in places the very old pair inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport

explanation.surface: An elderly person in a vehicle jumps around.
explanation.walkthrough: VO goes into CART.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap and caper about excitedly.

clue.text: Arbitrator takes turn with horse, one needing shelter

parts.note: a ref is a referee, an arbitrator
a U-turn, so U stands for turn
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A referee turns and rides off, looking for somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: GEE is short for gee-gee, nursery slang for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone fleeing danger who seeks asylum.

clue.text: Current application, genetically modified, in which almost all almost disappear

indicators.note: in which says GM wraps around the other letters
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the word all, shortened

indicators.note: the second almost also clips the final letter

parts.note: vanish means disappear

explanation.surface: A modified technique in which nearly everything nearly vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'almost' clips one following word by its final letter; 'in which' makes the GM abbreviation the outer shell. Luigi Galvani gave his name to current electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanism is the use of electric current, as in Galvani's experiments on frogs.

clue.text: Town near Manchester loses right to contribute to soup

indicators.note: loses means the letter is dropped from the town

parts.note: Stockport is a town near Manchester

explanation.surface: A town in north-west England gives up its rights to provide soup.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot simmers bones and vegetables to make stock, the base of soups.

clue.text: Time for logic? That leads to disloyalty

parts.note: reason is logical thinking

explanation.surface: It is time for clear thinking, which turns out to be betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest disloyalty.

clue.text: Intrepidity? Certainly not!

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking fright is the essence of bravery, while 'no fear!' is slang for a firm refusal.

clue.text: Western tree found nowhere else?

parts.note: holly is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A western tree that grows in no other place.
explanation.walkthrough: Something found nowhere else exists solely in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly means exclusively, so something there and nowhere else is there exclusively.

clue.text: See 1
One asking for food in pub

indicators.note: in means the food goes inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is food

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub begs for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is one who asks for alms.

clue.text: Noise made by Archbishop Cosmo?

parts.note: C is the initial of Cosmo
Cosmo Gordon Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury

explanation.surface: A sound produced by a famous churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942; C. Lang read as one word is a metallic noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound.

clue.text: Joint participation in thankless task

indicators.note: participation in suggests the letters take part within the word thankless

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in an unrewarding job.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between foot and leg.

clue.text: If disturbed, put back in hearth

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the two letters of if are knocked out of order

parts.note: to replace is to put back

explanation.surface: If anything is moved, return it to the fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace is the hearth where a fire burns.

clue.text: Old piece of animation including "The King and I" is from fellow continental

indicators.note: including means the old piece wraps around the king and I

parts.note: past means old or former

indicators.note: piece of means only part of the word animation is used

explanation.surface: An old cartoon features the musical The King and I and comes from a fellow continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' and 'and' in the musical's title are link words; only King and I give letters. A Pakistani is a fellow Asian to an Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Pakistan shares the Asian continent with, say, an Indian.

clue.text: It's better on cake than on aerofoils

definitions.text: It's better on cake than on aerofoils

parts.words: It's better on cake than on aerofoils
parts.note: a sugary topping on a cake is welcome, but frozen build-up on aircraft wings is dangerous

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sweet cake coating and ice forming on aircraft surfaces.

clue.text: Man of God commits model crime

parts.note: T as in the Model T Ford
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A churchman carries out a robbery as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous car.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is one who believes in God.

clue.text: Hourglass, small one, say — great one has some merit

parts.note: eg means for example, as does say
G is an abbreviation for great, as in grand

indicators.note: some here suggests a jumbled version of the word merit

explanation.surface: A small hourglass is the example; a large one has a certain value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' rearranges MERIT into TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sand-glass that times the boiling of eggs is a small hourglass.
